skills.before: The short invocation. Ask "have I seen this before?" about something you are looking at right now: duplicated logic, a parallel path, work that feels familiar while being written as new. Answers in seconds to minutes over a scope you name, and escalates to a full duplication audit when the scope warrants it. For the long invocation, a whole-codebase sweep of entry points whose consequences have drifted apart, use drydry:parity-audit.
skills.after: Check "have I seen this before?" for duplicated logic, parallel paths, or work that feels familiar while being written as new, in code, prose, or design. Escalate when needed; use parity-audit for a whole-codebase audit of divergent entry points.

skills.before: The long invocation. A multi-agent, whole-codebase sweep over every entry point that promises one outcome, to find where their consequences diverge, converge the difference into the shared path, and re-run the audit to prove it moved. Runs as a named background process over minutes, not seconds. For a quick "have I seen this code before?" check, use drydry:drydry instead.
skills.after: Audit every entry point promising the same outcome across a codebase, converge divergent consequences, and verify again. Runs as a named background multi-agent process; use drydry for a quick duplication check.

skills.after: Clarify unclear controls, state, consequences, inline/modal/page/cell placement, or over-explaining UI. plugins.before: Cuss at your coding agent to capture a one-line friction note, then fix the real problem later. The cuss commands (/fuck, /fucking, /fucked, /shit, /crap, /wtf, /bullshit) append one cheap line to a global log and move on; safeword commands (/safeword, /pineapple, /pineapplejuice, /pinapplejuice, /flugelhorn, /banana) interrupt current work and fix one visible friction point now without logging it for later. /anger-management:repair cools down (~22 min, a background headless agent investigates), reads the full capture history, scores confidence, chooses the mitigation layer and target scope, and only applies or routes a fix when confidence is high enough. Lower-confidence findings leave the breadcrumb trail open for a future pass. Modelled on Stripe's bad-day button, course-correction-before-escalation, and the constructed-emotion view of anger; sometimes the irritation is real, sometimes it is playful. Vocabulary avoids slurs and identity-targeted abuse. State is stored locally; the optional background investigation uses the configured runner.
plugins.after: Capture friction with /fuck, /fucking, /fucked, /shit, /crap, /wtf, or /bullshit for later background investigation. Fix now with /safeword, /pineapple, /pineapplejuice, /pinapplejuice, /flugelhorn, or /banana. /anger-management:repair reviews captured notes and applies or routes high-confidence fixes; /anger-management shows the tally. State stays local.
plugins.subtitle: Capture and repair friction

plugins.before: Keep an autonomous mission running across turns. plugins.after: Keep autonomous missions running across turns with a host capability probe, heartbeat backoff, auto-stop, and wake/restore where needed. Persistent hosts need no heartbeat machinery.

plugins.before: Single-occupancy lock for a git worktree or standalone working directory: a vendor-neutral, cross-platform CLI so only one coding agent mutates a repository checkout at a time. claim/release/check use an atomic exclusive-create lockfile keyed by the nearest git worktree root, falling back to directory realpath outside git, with pid-based liveness that self-heals a dead holder and respects a live one. No flock, no native dependency. bonsai and the discipline hooks consume it.
plugins.after: Claim, check, and release directory occupancy locks so coding agents do not mutate the same checkout concurrently. Vendor-neutral CLI with live-holder protection and stale-lock recovery.
plugins.subtitle: Coordinate directory writes

plugins.before: Find and converge parallel paths in any artefact: code, prose, design systems. Methodology guide that disciplines how a duplication audit runs (Type-4 clone framing, verifier-burden LLM pass, allow-list scoping, drift hypothesis, triage, two-fates discipline, contrarian second-pass, method-as-artefact) without prescribing what duplication looks like in your codebase. One orchestrator (drydry:drydry) with quick and audit modes; the calling session formulates the audit checklist from the codebase in front of it. Agent-only sub-skills handle sweep, checklist seeds, triage, research, upstream/framework checks, and instruction-file audits.
plugins.after: Find duplicated logic and parallel paths in code, prose, or design. Run a quick scoped check or a whole-codebase parity audit, then converge verified divergence and check the result.
plugins.subtitle: Find and converge duplication
